title: Investigate and fix per-route quota drift and double-enforcement in rate-limit policy engine
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported unexpected quota exhaustion and billing spikes. We observed quota counters drifting (per-route and per-org) with cases of double-enforcement where a single request consumed tokens from both per-key and per-org buckets incorrectly. This ticket tracks investigation, fix, tests, and rollout for the policy engine bug in the rate-limiter module.

Impact: High (customer-facing billing and quota correctness). Affected surfaces: hosted API, dedicated runtime when routing through policy-proxy, and console usage reports. Not all requests are impacted; appears correlated with legacy X-Org-Id header + concurrent optimistic cache writes during rolling policy reloads.

Goals: 1) Reproduce reliably in staging. 2) Patch policy engine to ensure atomic counter updates and single-source org resolution. 3) Add guardrails and e2e tests to prevent regressions. 4) Deploy with canary and monitor billing/usage metrics.

What we suspect: race between policy-cache reload and request evaluation causes evaluator to temporarily see both the per-key and per-org enforcement paths, leading to duplicated token accounting. Also a secondary code path merges route-level rules twice on fallback when a route rule is missing, incrementing the bucket twice.

Acceptance criteria: - No duplicate counter increments observed under stress tests. - Regression tests (unit + integration) covering cache reload + concurrent eval added. - Canary (10% of production requests) runs for 48 hours with no new customer incidents. - Post-rollout telemetry shows per-route/quota alignment to previous baseline within 1% variance.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Aisha Patel: Ticket created after first customer alert (customer: Acadia Analytics). Added initial logs and request traces to the incident channel.

2026-03-01 - Marco Reyes: Reproduced quota drift locally using synthetic load harness. Reproduction steps added to runbook. Observed duplicate increments when policy reload triggers while requests evaluate.
2026-03-03 - Priya Shah (PM): Noted this caused a billing spike for Acadia; coordinated with Finance to hold invoices pending investigation. Marking high priority for immediate fix.

2026-03-05 - Marco Reyes: Narrowed root cause to evaluator.mergeRules() being invoked twice for route fallbacks; also found non-atomic increments in accounting.Store.increment() when using the in-memory cache behind a short TTL.

2026-03-06 - Evan Liu (SRE): Added temporary mitigation: block policy reloads for 30s after deploy and disable optimistic parallel writes to accounting store in staging. Reduced incidents but not fully resolved.

2026-03-09 - Marco Reyes: Drafted hotfix branch (github.com/redwood-inference/policy-engine/pull/1423). Hotfix includes: 1) idempotent mergeRules; 2) compare-and-swap increments in accounting store; 3) safe org-resolution that prefers token-key header over legacy header. Added unit tests.

2026-03-10 - Grace Kim (Design): UX note: console shows inconsistent per-route usage during incidents. Will schedule a follow-up to display 'investigating' flag on affected routes in the Usage dashboard.
2026-03-11 - Marco Reyes: Integration tests added to CI that simulate concurrent reload + high-QPS evaluation (test file: tests/concurrency/reload_qps_test.go). Local CI passes; need staging run.
2026-03-12 - Marco Reyes: Deployed PR to staging with 10% canary traffic. Observed no duplicate increments in staging telemetry after 6 hours. Requested extended canary to 48 hours.
2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Finance confirmed held invoices for Acadia until fix deployment. Preparing customer communication template. Next steps: prod canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback plan.
notes: Workaround for customers: disable legacy X-Org-Id header or pin to dedicated key-based enforcement until fix is rolled out.
Longer-term: revisit cache TTL semantics and make policy reloads transactional with respect to evaluation.
